subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should mobile support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers for authenticating proxies, or should the supported native proxy-auth surface be limited to narrower typed credentials first?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent choice controls credential storage, redaction, TLS requirements, gateway-only isolation, and credentials sent before OpenClaw Gateway auth.

options.title: Approve arbitrary headers with safeguards
options.body: Land the Android and iOS slices after owner/security review confirms sanitizer rules, secure-store lifecycle, redaction, reset behavior, gateway-only attachment, and real proxy proof.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth
options.body: Require Basic/Bearer or fixed-header credential types instead of arbitrary name/value headers to reduce validation and UX risk.

options.title: Defer native proxy credentials
options.body: Keep mobile authenticated-proxy deployments unsupported for now and document VPN, Tailscale, WebChat, or proxy-bypass alternatives.

recommendation.title: Approve arbitrary headers with safeguards
recommendation.body: Land the Android and iOS slices after owner/security review confirms sanitizer rules, secure-store lifecycle, redaction, reset behavior, gateway-only attachment, and real proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the canonical issue and both linked platform implementation PRs, and his current-main history is on the central mobile gateway files.
